title: Zuppa di funghi
subtitle: Italian wild mushroom soup with porcini and thyme
excerpt: A deeply flavoured Italian mushroom soup built from a base of dried porcini and fresh chestnut mushrooms, sautéed with garlic and thyme, and finished as either a chunky broth or a smooth cream. Served with toasted bread rubbed with garlic.
sourceNotes: Zuppa di funghi is a classic Italian soup found throughout the mushroom-rich regions of Umbria, Tuscany, and Piedmont. It appears in Ada Boni's Il Talismano della Felicità (1929) and in multiple Italian regional cooking references from Artusi onwards. The combination of dried porcini for depth and fresh mushrooms for texture is standard.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding cream (if making the creamy version). The chunky version freezes well.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made 2 days ahead and reheated. The flavour improves over time.

content.text: The key to a good zuppa di funghi is the dried porcini. They provide an intensity and depth of mushroom flavour that fresh mushrooms alone cannot match: the soaking liquid becomes part of the soup, and its dark, earthy concentration carries through every bowl. Using a mix of dried porcini for flavour and fresh chestnut mushrooms for body and texture is the most reliable approach when fresh wild mushrooms are not available.

items.prepNote: soaked in 300 ml warm water for 20 minutes; soaking liquid reserved
clove, halved, for rubbing the toast

content.text: Lift the soaked porcini out of their liquid. Roughly chop them. Carefully pour the soaking liquid through a fine sieve or through kitchen paper into a jug, leaving any grit behind. Reserve the liquid.

Heat the olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 6 minutes until soft. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute. Add the chopped fresh mushrooms and soaked porcini, raise the heat to high, and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until the mushrooms have released their liquid and the pan is almost dry again.
Add the white wine and let it bubble until reduced by half. Pour in the stock and the reserved porcini soaking liquid. Bring to the boil and simmer for 20 minutes. Remove the thyme sprigs.

For a chunky soup: season well, scatter with parsley, and serve with toasted bread that has been rubbed with the cut garlic clove. For a smooth soup: blend, return to the pan, season, and serve the same way.

items.cause: Porcini soaking liquid added without straining, or porcini not fully rinsed
items.fix: Always strain the porcini liquid through a fine sieve or kitchen paper. The grit from dried porcini is hard to remove once it is in the soup.

content.text: Wild mushroom soup belongs to the Italian mountain regions where mushroom picking is a serious autumn activity. Umbria, Tuscany, Piedmont, and the Trentino are its heartland. The porcini (Boletus edulis) is the most prized species. Where it grows abundantly, the soup is made with fresh porcini alone. Outside mushroom season, dried porcini combined with fresh cultivated mushrooms is the standard approach.
